why: Corrections to the genai-prices catalog, checked against the vendor's own pricing page. An override beats the catalog and loses to a human's `cci price set`. Each entry says what the catalog gets wrong, where the right number came from, and when someone last looked; delete an entry once upstream agrees. Rates are the vendor's five columns collapsed to ours: base input, 5m cache write, 1h cache write, cache hit, output. Same matcher language as model_prices.json, first match wins, and a matcher must not be broader than the model it corrects -- `claude-fable-5-1` and `claude-fable-5` differ only in cache reads, and a rule that caught both would reintroduce the error it exists to fix.

models.why: The catalog has no entry of its own for Fable 5.1 and matches it to `claude-fable-5`, whose cache reads cost four times as much ($1 against $0.25 per MTok). Fable 5.1 prices cache hits at 0.025x base input where every other model uses 0.1x. On a corpus where cache reads are 59% of the bill that single substitution was worth $2,752, or 21% of the total.
Limited availability, so the catalog does not carry it at all and its traffic would be reported unpriced. The vendor lists it at Fable 5.1's rates, cheap cache hits included.
As above, at Claude Fable 5's rates -- standard 0.1x cache hits, not Fable 5.1's 0.025x.

The catalog carries a price rise on 2026-09-01 to $3/$15 that did not happen: those are Claude Sonnet 4.6's rates. The vendor still lists Sonnet 5 at $2/$10 with $0.20 cache hits. Worth $4.73 here, and wrong in a way that grows with every Sonnet 5 hour.
